from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "A vector is a physical reality.",
            "A basis is a language.",
            "Different bases describe the same vector.",
            "We use grids as our frame.",
            "Coordinates change, but reality stays."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Intuition: Same Reality, Different Maps", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        grid_a = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"color": "#FF0000"}).scale(0.4)
        grid_b = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"color": "#00FF00"}).scale(0.4).rotate(30*DEGREES)
        point = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        point_marker = Circle(radius=0.1, color=WHITE)
        eq = MathTex(r"V_B = M \cdot V_A", font_size=30)
        
        self.place_at_grid(grid_a, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(grid_b, 'B5')
        self.place_at_grid(point, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(point_marker, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(eq, 'E4')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_a), FadeIn(grid_b), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(point), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(Create(point_marker), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(Write(eq), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Transformation Matrix", [
            "We relate two distinct bases.",
            "Basis vectors map to coordinates.",
            "These form the transformation matrix.",
            "Matrix P bridges our views.",
            "Conversion relies on matrix multiplication."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Define basis vectors i and j for System A (#FF0000)
        i_vec = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT, color="#FF0000")
        j_vec = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(i_vec, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(j_vec, 'C2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(i_vec), Create(j_vec))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF0000")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show how i and j map to new positions in B
        i_new = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT + 0.5 * UP, color="#00FF00")
        j_new = Arrow(ORIGIN, -0.5 * RIGHT + UP, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(i_new, 'B4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(j_new, 'C4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(i_vec.copy(), i_new), ReplacementTransform(j_vec.copy(), j_new))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Construct a 2x2 grid representing Matrix M
        matrix_m = MathTex(r"P = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -0.5 \\ 0.5 & 1 \end{pmatrix}", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_m, 'E3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(matrix_m))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Show column vectors of M as transformed basis vectors
        self.play(Indicate(matrix_m), run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Pulse Matrix M to emphasize its role as a bridge
        self.play(matrix_m.animate.scale(1.1).set_color("#FFFFFF"), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(matrix_m.animate.scale(1/1.1).set_color("#FFFF00"), run_time=0.5)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FFFF")

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Step-by-Step Computational Workflow", [
            "Express old basis in new.", 
            "Construct the transition matrix P.", 
            "Multiply to convert the coordinates."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        vec_x = MathTex(r"\mathbf{x} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}", color="#FF0000")
        mat_p = MathTex(r"P = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}", color="#00FF00")
        vec_y = MathTex(r"\mathbf{y} = P \mathbf{x} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}", color="#00AAFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(vec_x, "B2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(vec_x))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.place_at_grid(mat_p, "B5", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(mat_p))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.place_at_grid(vec_y, "E4", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(vec_y))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00AAFF")
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis and Visualization", [
            "Changing basis shifts our perspective.",
            "The physical object remains constant.",
            "Coordinates are just numerical representations."
        ])
        
        # Grid setup
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_numbers": False})
        self.place_in_area(grid, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(grid)
        
        # Point P
        p = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        p.move_to(grid.c2p(1.5, 1.0))
        label_p = Text("P", color=YELLOW, font_size=20).next_to(p, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        # Basis vectors
        b1 = Vector(grid.c2p(1, 0) - grid.c2p(0, 0), color=BLUE)
        b2 = Vector(grid.c2p(0, 1) - grid.c2p(0, 0), color=RED)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Create(b1), Create(b2), FadeIn(p), Write(label_p))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        
        # Transform basis to show perspective shift
        new_b1 = Vector(grid.c2p(0.5, 0.8) - grid.c2p(0, 0), color=BLUE)
        new_b2 = Vector(grid.c2p(-0.8, 0.5) - grid.c2p(0, 0), color=RED)
        
        # Animate grid and basis change
        grid_new = grid.copy()
        grid_new.apply_matrix([[0.5, -0.8], [0.8, 0.5]])
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(grid, grid_new),
            ReplacementTransform(b1, new_b1),
            ReplacementTransform(b2, new_b2)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Understanding Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: The Intuition: Same Reality, Different Maps
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a coordinate system as a 'language' to describe a vector. Establish the prerequisite: A basis is a set of linearly independent vectors that span the space. Use a visual of a squirrel (the vector) needing to be located on a grid. Different observers (bases) use different 'units' to describe the same squirrel.
sections.example: A squirrel sits at point (3, 2) in a standard grid. If a bird sees the world through a stretched, tilted grid, it perceives the same squirrel at different coordinates.

sections.title: Defining the Transformation Matrix
sections.content: Explain how to bridge two bases (B and C). Represent the basis vectors of B as coordinates within basis C. These columns form the Change-of-Basis Matrix (P). Use an animation where basis vectors slide and rotate to align with the new coordinate system.
sections.example: If basis B = {b1, b2} and basis C = {c1, c2}, the matrix P is [ [b1]c | [b2]c ]. Applying P converts a vector 'v' from B-coordinates to C-coordinates: [v]c = P[v]b.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Computational Workflow
sections.content: Provide a clear, algorithmic approach: 1. Express the 'old' basis vectors in terms of the 'new' basis. 2. Arrange these as columns to form the transition matrix P. 3. Multiply the original coordinate vector by P.
sections.example: Translating a robot's arm position from 'Global World Coordinates' to 'Arm-Segment Local Coordinates' using a 2x2 transition matrix.

sections.title: Synthesis and Visualization
sections.content: Consolidate the concept: Changing basis is a 'perspective shift,' not a change in the vector's actual position in space. The vector is the physical object; the coordinates are just the numerical representation based on our chosen 'ruler'.
sections.example: A video game character (the vector) remains in the same spot, but changing the camera view (the basis) changes how the game engine calculates the character's position on the screen.
